subject: Starter credit & early-ramp concession request — PulseArc Health
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Starter credit & early-ramp concession request — PulseArc Health

Team,

Quick thread — PulseArc (enterprise health prospect) has verbally committed to a 12-month Dedicated contract with a ~1.2M annualized ARR expectation if we can soften their ramp economics for the first 90 days. They are asking for a one-off starter credit that effectively offsets usage while they onboard heavy imaging workloads.

Why this matters:
- Large strategic logos in our healthcare vertical accelerate both seats and Dedicated adoption in region-warranted clouds.
- They’re sensitive to first-month spikes (integration + model-tuning) and have a narrow procurement window — legal wants a signed SOW by 10/30.
- If we decline, they will default to a cloud provider bundle; if we accept we lock a multi-year placement and potential marketplace resell.

Ask: I’m requesting VP/CFO clearance for a structured starter credit up to $60,000 applied over the first 90 days, with the following guardrails:
- Credit applied only to token/throughput overage for onboarding spikes (explicit line item in SOW).
- PulseArc signs a 12-month Dedicated commitment with 6-figure monthly minimums after the ramp quarter.
- Standard breakage clauses and no-retroactive refunds; credit non-transferable.

Attachments: PulseArc_MA_plans.xlsx (usage forecast + ramp profile), proposal-v2.pdf (redlines highlighted).

Notes: Finance model in the spreadsheet shows NPV-neutral after month 4 if we keep baseline rate card and enforce minimums. I’ve included a short commercial summary in the spreadsheet.

Marissa / Marcus — can you weigh in on finance tolerance and whether we need a reduced cap or alternative structure (e.g., time-limited credits + milestone-based tranche)? Karthik — can you confirm if this requires any exec memo besides CFO sign-off?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Starter credit & early-ramp concession request — PulseArc Health

Vanessa — thanks for the context and the files. Quick reactions:

- $60k over 90 days is on the higher side but not unreasonable if the ARR and commit are solid and we protect against churn.
- I need to see a clearer monthly minimum schedule in the SOW; the spreadsheet shows a wide range and procurement will lock to the lower end unless we make minimums explicit.
- Put measurable milestones for credit release. E.g., 30% of credit released after first successful production inference run and 70% released in two equal tranches tied to MAU/inference volume thresholds.
- We should include an audit clause for usage validation to prevent accidental over-crediting.

If Marcus and Karthik are comfortable, I’ll draft a two-paragraph memo for the CFO summarizing the ask and the financial mitigations. That should be enough for sign-off.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Agree with Marissa. A couple of additional points from a commercial/ops perspective:

- Recommend capping credit at what our model shows as onboarding delta (I ran numbers — $45k covers their expected spike with a small buffer). If we must do $60k, condition X must be met (signed minimums + DSAT protection).
- Insert a clause that credits expire if they pause production or if usage falls below the agreed minimum for two consecutive billing periods.
- Ops will need a tracking tag in their account to isolate credited usage for reporting — I can have the runtime team implement that tag after legal signs the SOW.

If Marissa drafts the CFO memo, I’ll add the operational gating language and the cap recommendation.

Thanks,

Vanessa / Marissa / Marcus — copied Emma (PulseArc) so we’re transparent on next steps.

From a sign-off standpoint: CFO clearance required; Marissa, please send the short memo (summary + mitigations). I am OK to endorse up to $50,000 in starter credit with the following executive conditions:

1) PulseArc signs the 12-month Dedicated SOW with a minimum monthly commitment at or above the "baseline" in the spreadsheet.
2) Credits are milestone-gated as Marissa suggested (30% / 35% / 35%).
3) Credit cap set to $50,000; any request above that requires a brief exec email to CFO with explicit justification.
4) We include usage audit & expiration clauses, and an account-tagging requirement from Ops.

Emma — appreciate the urgency. If PulseArc is comfortable with the $50k structure and the milestone gating, we can fast-track the SOW and get legal/finance sign-off by Friday. If you’d like, Vanessa can schedule a quick 20-minute walkthrough of the milestones so we can finalize language.

Thanks,
